newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: TENNIS-BECKER RETURNS WITH A WIN AT SWISS INDOORS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BECKER RETURNS WITH A WIN AT SWISS INDOORS.

text.p: Boris Becker returned successfully to competition on Tuesday beating the Czech Republic's Bohdan Ulihrach at the Swiss Indoor tournament after three months sidelined with a wrist injury.

After an aborted comeback attempt at a tournament in Bucharest two weeks ago, Becker's damaged right wrist stood the test as he fought past Ulihrach, ranked a respectable 36 in the world, 6-1 5-7 6-3.
It was the Australian Open champion's first complete match since rupturing a tendon in the wrist during third round play at Wimbledon.
"I'm satisfied to get through," said Becker, who had lost to Ulihrach earlier this year at an indoor event in Milan. "I had good concentration but I lost it a bit in the second set.
"I may feel pretty stiff tomorrow after having not played for such a long time.
"I'm not as fit as I was before the injury."
After a quick start Becker began to show signs of his long layoff as his booming serve often deserted him, particularly in the second set.
But the fourth seed and world number six recovered quickly, breaking Ulihrach early in the third to take control of the decisive set 3-0.
"I had to use my injured wrist to control my serves and it's not strong enough yet to hit really hard," said Becker.

Sixth seed Stefan Edberg, who helped Sweden to a Davis Cup semifinal win over the Czech Republic on the weekend, also advanced but struggled to get past last year's finalist Jan Siemerink of the Netherlands 6-3 5-7 6-3.
Arnaud Boetsch, who capped France's comeback victory over Italy in the other Davis Cup semifinal, withdrew on Tuesday with a sore back.
His replacement, Germany's Marc Goellner, took advantage of the opportunity disposing of Boetsch's Davis Cup teammate Guy Forget 6-7 (7-4) 6-4 6-4.
World number one Pete Sampras will see his first action since winning the U.S. Open title on Wednesday when the American takes on qualifier Alex Radulescu of Germany.
